Because.title: Because

BusinessTypeProfile.title: BusinessTypeProfile
BusinessTypeProfile.description:
Gemini proposes this from owner words/menu/photos; approval still belongs to the owner.

A single envelope keeps the ADK tool schema simple; only the matching typed block is valid.
Missing profiles are version 1 generic, without guessing anything about existing records.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: product (sells goods), service (does work for people), food (food or drink to eat), mixed (two of these), unknown (not clear yet)

what.title: What
what.description: What it is, in the owner's words

customer_wants.title: Customer Wants
customer_wants.description: What a customer would want to know

BusinessUnderstanding.title: BusinessUnderstanding
BusinessUnderstanding.description: What the coach understood about the business, from the owner's own words.

Command.title: Command
Command.description:
A customer command answered at once, by voice or text: my stamps, directions to a shop,
follow a shop, ask a shop's owner. Following and asking still happen on the shop's page.

source_label.title: Source Label
source_label.description: E.g. Petpooja, Tally, Square, Shopify, SAP, Other

ConnectorMapping.title: ConnectorMapping
ConnectorMapping.description: Complete mapping from an external system export to the Chalkboard schema.

preview_rows.title: Preview Rows
preview_rows.description: First 5 rows mapped to our schema

ConnectorResult.title: ConnectorResult
ConnectorResult.description: What we return to the frontend after parsing + AI mapping.

CustomFact.title: CustomFact
CustomFact.description: A fact this kind of business's customers ask about (e.g. a salon's walk-in policy).

Day.title: Day
Day.description: One shop day. ``None`` means "no record", never zero.

question.title: Question
question.description: How to ask the owner, plain English

source_field.title: Source Field
source_field.description: Original column/field name from the export

target_field.title: Target Field
target_field.description: Our schema field: name, price, unit, stock, quantity, date, total, category

FieldMapping.title: FieldMapping
FieldMapping.description: One source → target column mapping produced by Gemini or confirmed by the owner.

Intent.title: Intent
Intent.description: What the customer asked for. Prices are in the local currency's major units.

NextReward.title: NextReward
NextReward.description: The single next named reward ("2 more stamps → free bun maska").

Personal.title: Personal
Personal.description: What the signed-in customer's profile changed: never applied when signed out.

PickDeal.title: PickDeal
PickDeal.description: A live closing-time rescue on this shop (demo rescues are labelled).

Playbook.title: Playbook
Playbook.description: Bounded on purpose: a playbook is a short page the owner can read in a minute.

price.title: Price
price.description: Minor units of the shop currency; integer, never a float

Pulse.title: Pulse
Pulse.description: One day's activity; None means "no record", never zero.

until.title: Until
until.description: Today's pickup deadline in shop-local HH:MM; no overnight deals

RuleSet.title: RuleSet
RuleSet.description: What the owner edits (screen or coach). Money is in minor units of the shop currency.

ScratchView.title: ScratchView
ScratchView.description:
A scratch card. Before it is scratched, the prize stays on the server; the odds that
apply to this card are always shown.

ShopGames.title: ShopGames
ShopGames.description: What a shop page shows about its games, signed in or not.

note.title: Note
note.default: Estimate assumes saved stock is opening prepared quantity; confirm what remains. Missing sales or closing hours prevents an estimate.

pulse.title: Pulse
pulse.description: Pulse numbers to show first (Today.Pulse keys)

TodayHints.title: TodayHints
TodayHints.description: What the Today page personalises. It only shows what exists; these only set the order.

Understanding.title: Understanding
Understanding.description:
The owner's own answers to "what matters most now" and "who are your regulars". Private:
it shapes the shop playbook and never appears in any customer projection. Busiest times are
the existing busy_hours fact (customers benefit from it too).
